chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the Zakat al-Fitr.
He said: Give charity on behalf of all those you provide for, whether young or old, free or slave. For every person, half a sa' of wheat or one sa' of barley, and the sa' is four mudds.

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: Mudds (a smaller unit of volume, 1 sa' = 4 mudds)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (Charity of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the required amount and who must pay Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *al-Istibsar* clarifies the universal scope of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing that the obligation extends to all dependents—whether children, adults, free, or enslaved—under the payer's care. It establishes the specific volumetric measurements of half a sa' of wheat or a full sa' of barley, with the sa' defined as four mudds, reflecting the practical economic realities of Medina during the early Imams. This ruling underscores the social welfare dimension of the ritual, ensuring the poor are nourished at the conclusion of Ramadan.
